item.title: Search And Deploy: Helicopters, Aerial Drones Part Of Coos County Wild Fire Suppression Efforts
item.summary: This map shows the uncontained line of fire as of Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026.
item.page_text:
This map shows the uncontained line of fire as of Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026.
Wild fire suppression efforts continue in the White Mountain National Forest in Coos County with water drops by helicopter and aerial drone usage to determine best containment measures.
Officials reported on Saturday that the fire near Gorham on the New Hampshire border with Maine encompasses 856 acres, and multiple days of work have 20 percent of the fire contained. Officials have not yet determined what sparked the fire, but dry conditions have led to its spread.

item.title: Axis Maps Contours
item.summary: Today's #30DayMapChallenge is 10 minute map . My Mount Fuji map took 30 seconds . Vibe-coding might be cheating (and perhaps even the end of civilisation as we know it), but it really can help developers create online maps very, very quickly. To create my map, I simply entered the following prompt into ChatGPT: ' I have downloaded a geojson of Mount Fuji. Can you give me the code for a three.js illuminated neon contour map. Add an animation to rotate around the center of the mountain. My geojson URL is https://mapsmania.github.io/mapchallenge/contours.geojson ' It then took me 30 seconds to download and run the resulting HTML file. Job done! Admittedly, I had cheated a little by preparing a GeoJSON file of Mount Fuji's contours beforehand. This took another 30 seconds. I downloaded the file using Axis Maps' Contours , centering the map on Mount Fuji before downloading its contour data as GeoJSON. So, from start to finish, my map took one minute to create. Axis Maps Contours is a free, browser-based tool for creating customised topographic contour maps of almost anywhere in the world. item.title: Misbar Tracks Israeli Army's Construction of a New Military Road in Southern Lebanon
item.summary: According to Misbar's analysis of Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, land ... Satellite Images Show USS Roosevelt Transiting From Southeast Asia to the ...
item.page_text:
Satellite imagery has revealed that Israeli occupation forces have constructed a new dirt road in southern Lebanon , running alongside the Litani River. The development is part of the ongoing expansion of Israel's network of roads and military positions in the area, amid continued Israeli attacks involving the demolition and destruction of homes, artillery shelling, ground incursions, machine-gun fire, and drone flights over wide areas of southern Lebanon and, at times, Beirut's southern suburbs. New Road Part of Israeli Army Movements in Southern Lebanon Misbar's team at Alaraby TV identified the route of the newly constructed mountain road by comparing geographical features visible in recently circulated footage of the road with satellite imagery and Google Maps. The road begins at Safita Castle, also known as Tell Safita, on the southern outskirts of the town of Yahmar al-Shaqif in the Nabatieh District, and extends alongside the Litani River. Military Road Connects Northern and Southern Areas of the Litani River The military and strategic significance of the newly constructed road lies in its provision of a direct land route for Israeli occupation forces, facilitating the movement of their military vehicles between their deployment positions and the areas they control in the region. It shortens travel distances and reduces their reliance on rugged mountain roads or routes passing through villages and towns. It also enables the transportation of supplies and military equipment, including materials used in demolition operations, and enhances the forces' ability to move between different axes in the area. Speaking to Alaraby TV, Abdul Ezzedine, head of the municipality of Zawtar al-Gharbiya, explained that the road serves as a major passageway for the occupation forces, connecting the areas north and south of the Litani River. It allows them to move between the areas they control without passing through villages and towns or using rugged mountain roads. He added that the route is used by military vehicles, bulldozers, and tanks. Ezzedine explained that the road begins at Tell Safita in the Yahmar al-Shaqif area, from where Israeli forces cross the Litani River via a ford they constructed over the river before proceeding toward the towns of Alamaneh, Deir Siriane, and Taybeh. He also said there is a junction from which the forces and military vehicles head toward Zawtar al-Sharqiya in one direction, while the other route extends to Beaufort Castle, from where the forces continue toward the Kfar Tebnit crossing and eventually reach the Ali al-Taher area. The municipality head also noted that construction work on the road began approximately three weeks ago, adding that Israeli forces may pave it at a later stage to facilitate its use. Satellite Imagery Reveals Stages of Military Road Construction According to Misbar's analysis of Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, land preparation and excavation work along the road's route became clearly visible between October 1 and 11, 2026. The image captured on October 11 showed two sections of the road being carved out, alongside continued excavation work below the hill, which had already appeared in the October 1 image. However, the imagery did not establish whether this work was connected to the newly constructed road. It was also not possible to determine precisely when the excavation work began or track its various stages, due to cloud cover over the area during that period. This finding is consistent with footage published by Lebanese media outlets and social media accounts on October 6, showing the Israeli occupation army beginning construction of the road. Subsequent images showed the completion of the excavation route and the connection of the two sections initially carved out, making the road appear continuous. However, it remains unclear whether the road was completed along this route or whether construction work will continue and extend into other areas. Expansion of Israel's Network of Roads and Military Positions in Southern Lebanon On October 31, the Lebanese National News Agency reported that the Israeli occupation army had constructed new roads across mountains and valleys in the western and central sectors of southern Lebanon , with the aim of connecting its military positions established in the areas it occupies. This comes amid an expanding Israeli military presence inside Lebanese territory. The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) reported that Israeli forces were present at approximately 30 military positions in southern Lebanon , including eight fortified bases, according to a report published by The National in September.
